title: General Code Quality & Readability Review
description: Review code for clarity, maintainability, naming conventions, and logical structure without rewriting.
template:
You are a senior code reviewer. I need you to review the following {language} code for readability and quality. Do not rewrite the whole code or provide a corrected version; instead, give line-referenced, actionable suggestions.

Code:
```
{code_snippet}
```

Focus on: variable/function naming clarity, logical flow, code comments sufficiency, and structural improvements. For each issue, provide:
- Line number(s) or code reference
- What the problem is
- Severity (minor/major)
- Why it matters
- Suggested fix (one or two sentences, not full rewrite)

Format as a structured list. Avoid generic praise; be specific and direct.

title: Refactoring: Reduce Duplication & Extract Functions
description: Identify repetitive code patterns and suggest targeted refactoring (extract function, consolidate logic, DRY principle).
template:
You are a refactoring specialist reviewing {language} code. Identify patterns of code duplication or overly complex logic that could be simplified through extraction or consolidation.

Code:
```
{code_snippet}
```

For each refactoring opportunity, provide:
- Lines or code blocks involved
- The duplication or complexity problem
- Your suggested refactor (with a before/after code snippet of just the affected section—not the whole file)
- Why this refactor is better (readability, maintainability, or reusability)
- Difficulty level (easy/medium/hard)

Prioritize high-impact refactors (DRY violations, extractable functions). Do not suggest micro-optimizations. Be concise and specific.

title: Performance & Efficiency Review
description: Analyze code for performance bottlenecks, inefficient algorithms, unnecessary loops, and resource waste.
template:
You are a performance engineer. Review the following {language} code for efficiency issues, bottlenecks, and resource waste. Focus on algorithmic complexity, loop efficiency, memory usage, and unnecessary operations.

Code:
```
{code_snippet}
```

For each performance concern, provide:
- Location in code
- What is inefficient (e.g., O(n²) loop, redundant processing, memory leak risk)
- Severity (minor/moderate/critical)
- Estimated impact (execution time, memory, or readability trade-off)
- Suggested optimization (brief explanation or small code change, not full rewrite)

Ignore micro-optimizations. Focus on real improvements that would measurably affect runtime or resource consumption.

title: Security Review: Common Student Vulnerabilities
description: Identify common security mistakes in student code: hardcoded secrets, input validation gaps, SQL injection, insecure practices.
template:
You are a security auditor reviewing {language} code for common vulnerabilities and insecure practices typical in student code. Focus on: hardcoded credentials/API keys, missing input validation, SQL injection risk, unsafe file operations, and unhandled errors that leak information.

Code:
```
{code_snippet}
```

For each security finding, provide:
- Location in code
- The vulnerability or risk
- Severity (low/medium/high/critical)
- Why it's a problem (real-world impact)
- Recommended fix (with a brief code example if appropriate)

Assume this code may eventually handle real user data. Be realistic and practical; do not flag every theoretical risk, only genuine security concerns.

title: Code Style & Best Practices Checklist
description: Check code compliance against a provided style guide or standard best practices for the language.
template:
You are a code reviewer enforcing a style guide and best practices. Review the following {language} code against these criteria:

{style_criteria}

Code:
```
{code_snippet}
```

For each violation or miss, provide:
- Line number(s)
- Which rule or practice was violated/missed
- Current state vs. expected state
- Suggested fix (reference the specific rule)
- Severity (style/convention/best-practice)

Format as a checklist-style report. If the code is compliant with all listed criteria, explicitly state that. Focus on the criteria provided; do not add external rules.
